member.name: T:nPianoFingering.FingeringSession
member.summary:
Incremental fingering for an editor. Keep one session per part and call with the whole part after every edit: the notes are compared with the previous call, only a region around the edit is analysed again, and every other note gets its previous hand and finger back. A single edit in a part of a few thousand notes takes milliseconds instead of a full run.
The run region is the edited range widened by onset groups on each side (cut at a rest when there is one, so the search starts and ends in a natural place); results are written only for the edited range widened by groups, so the region's own edges never leak into the result.
Not thread safe: use a session from one thread at a time (a background worker is fine).

member.summary: Splits a piano part into left and right hand. Every onset group is split at one point (lower notes to the left hand), and the sequence of splits is optimised with a beam search. member.name: T:nPianoFingering.FingerSpan
member.summary: Finger-pair span limits in semitones, after Parncutt et al. (1997), "An ergonomic model of keyboard fingering for melodic fragments", as used by Jacobs (2001) and Al Kasimi et al. (2007). Distances are measured from the lower-numbered finger to the higher-numbered finger, positive towards the little finger (up for the right hand, down for the left hand). A negative value means a crossing (thumb under / finger over).
